close_reason:
Added #[non_exhaustive] to CollisionError. Aligns with workspace pattern set by jmap_mail_types::KeywordError + foundation error types (JmapError, MethodResponseError, SetError). Pre-1.0 v0.1.x — no external semver impact.

Did NOT reshape struct -> enum per the bead's secondary 'consider' note; the bead lists it as 'a less critical divergence than the #[non_exhaustive] one' and the struct shape is well-justified (a Vec<String> payload + Display impl produces the right error semantics; the enum form would be a single-variant enum which adds no real type-system value).

Rustdoc-link gotcha: the doc-comment originally used [`jmap_mail_types::KeywordError`] intra-doc syntax, but contacts-types does not depend on mail-types. Changed to plain backticks so RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" still passes.

Workspace cargo test, clippy, rustdoc all clean.
description:
**Files**:
- crate-jmap-contacts-types/src/lib.rs — \`pub struct CollisionError { keys: Vec<String> }\` (private field, no \`#[non_exhaustive]\`)
- crate-jmap-mail-types/src/lib.rs — \`#[non_exhaustive] pub enum KeywordError { Empty, InvalidChar(char), ReservedPrefix }\`

**Divergence**: The two only crate-defined error types in the 8 extension type crates use opposite shapes:
- contacts: struct with private field, NO forward-compat annotation
- mail: enum with named variants, WITH \`#[non_exhaustive]\`

**What goes wrong**:
1. Adding a field to \`CollisionError\` (e.g. \`account_id: AccountId\` to disambiguate cross-account collisions) is a breaking change unless \`#[non_exhaustive]\` is added now. Same crate is at v0.1.1 — pre-1.0 so still cheap to fix.
2. Adding a variant to \`KeywordError\` (e.g. an out-of-range Unicode codepoint) is non-breaking because of \`#[non_exhaustive]\`.
3. Pattern divergence: a future error type in a third type crate (e.g. when sharing or filenode grows a validation-error class) won't know which template to mirror.

**Fix**: add \`#[non_exhaustive]\` to \`CollisionError\`. If the workspace's policy is 'error types are enums', also consider reshaping \`CollisionError\` to enum form (\`enum CollisionError { Duplicate { keys: Vec<String> } }\`) for symmetry with \`KeywordError\`, though the struct vs enum is a less critical divergence than the \`#[non_exhaustive]\` one.

**Related**: AGENTS.md ratifies \`#[non_exhaustive]\` on every public wire struct and on all wire-format result enums. The workspace does not explicitly cover crate-defined error types, but the precedent in \`KeywordError\` and \`JmapError\`/\`MethodResponseError\`/\`SetError\` (all \`#[non_exhaustive]\`) makes the implicit policy clear.
title: contacts-types `CollisionError` is a `pub struct` without `#[non_exhaustive]`, vs sibling `KeywordError` (mail-types) which is a `#[non_exhaustive] pub enum`
